01
Georgia has caught up to the national economy
After running a persistent unemployment-rate gap above the US for most of the post-GFC era, Georgia now matches or beats the national rate in any given month. The state ranks in the top quartile for job market health.
02
Participation is still the soft spot
Labor force participation in Georgia continues to trail the US by roughly half a percentage point. That's a structural ceiling on growth — there are workers on the sidelines that hiring alone won't reach.
03
HMGMA is reshaping coastal Georgia
Hyundai's $7.6B EV plant in Bryan County, announced May 2022 and opened October 2024, is already moving local indicators. Construction, manufacturing, and total payrolls in Savannah have all accelerated since the announcement. See Section 03.

Section 03

HMGMA — Hyundai's $7.6B EV bet on coastal Georgia

Announced May 2022. Groundbreaking October 2022. Plant opened October 2024. 8,500 direct jobs targeted at full ramp. This section tracks the three things that matter for an economic-development audience: whether the local labor market can supply the workers, whether Hyundai can compete on wages, and what the early signals look like in Savannah's labor market.

Section 04

Auto-industry peers — what does maturity look like?

Savannah is at the start of an auto-anchored economic transition. Four other Southeast metros went through this decades ago: Spartanburg (BMW since 1994), Tuscaloosa (Mercedes since 1997), Montgomery (Hyundai HMMA since 2005), and Charleston (Volvo since 2018). Their trajectories show what "mature" looks like — and what Savannah may look like in 2034.
